issues.description: There is a major contradiction regarding the timing of the intervention. The rationale states the intervention is placed BEFORE collaborative recall to 'inoculate' participants, but the Procedure section and Figure 2 description place it AFTER collaborative recall.
issues.quote: we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase... vs ...The procedure will consist of four main phases: (1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall... (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability.

issues.description: The manuscript contradicts itself regarding the format of the final memory test. Section 2.5 describes an open-ended test, while Section 3 (Analysis Plan) states it will use a two-alternative forced-choice (2AFC) format.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions... vs ...In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.description: The power analysis acknowledges that for a small effect size in the interaction (Cohen f = .10), 664 participants are needed. With only 240 participants, the study is severely underpowered to detect anything other than large effects, increasing the risk of Type II errors.
issues.quote: the required sample sizes for the small, medium, and large effects were 664, 112, and 48 participants, respectively... a sample of 240 participants was assumed.

issues.description: The 'Demonstration and motivation' group receives two distinct interventions (DRM task feedback and a motivational podcast), whereas other groups receive only one. If this group shows an effect, it is impossible to determine which component caused it.
issues.quote: it consists of two elements: (1) directly demonstrating the fallibility of memory... and (2) motivating them to provide correct answers.

issues.description: The DRM paradigm measures associative internal memory errors (false recall of related words), while the MORI technique measures social conformity to external misinformation. Using DRM to 'demonstrate' vulnerability to social misinformation lacks construct alignment.
issues.quote: The demonstration of the fallibility of memory will be done by means of the DRM technique.

issues.description: The authors hypothesize that the methods will be most effective for participants 'aware of discrepancies,' yet they provide no measure or analysis plan to identify or categorize these participants.
issues.quote: we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware.

issues.description: The power analysis assumes a correlation of 0.07 between repeated measures. This is exceptionally low for memory tests on the same material, which usually show high correlations. An incorrect correlation parameter invalidates the sample size calculation.
issues.quote: A correlation r = 0.07 between repeated measures was assumed based on the research described above.

issues.description: The control group listens to a podcast on 'soft skills,' which is not a 'memory' task. This fails to control for the effects of thinking about memory or the 'demand characteristics' of being told a study is about memory.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: For open-ended questions, there is no mention of who will code the data, whether they will be blind to the experimental condition, or how inter-rater reliability will be assessed.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers...

issues.description: The authors claim normative impact is 'completely ruled out' because the test is individual. This ignores the possibility of private acceptance (internalization) where a participant adopts the partner's view to avoid the internal discomfort of being 'wrong' or 'different.'
issues.quote: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own.

issues.description: The age range (16-35) is restricted, and the recruitment via media/internet likely targets a specific socio-economic or educational demographic, limiting the generalizability to the broader population of eyewitnesses (e.g., elderly or children).
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.description: The exclusion criteria for 'technical problems' is not pre-defined, allowing researchers to selectively exclude pairs if their data does not fit the hypothesis.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: The manuscript does not specify if the 4 critical details chosen for discussion are the same for all participants or if they are counterbalanced across the 8 possible details to avoid item-specific effects.
issues.quote: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.description: The IMP framework was designed for impersonal misinformation. Applying it to memory conformity without accounting for social dynamics (trust, power, gender in dyads) is a conceptual leap not fully justified.
issues.quote: The IMP was developed in the context of the classic misinformation paradigm... However, similar processes may apply to the memory conformity paradigm.

issues.description: The 'Demonstration' group is explicitly told 'you were fooled,' which may create a strong demand effect where participants feel they must be more skeptical than the other groups to please the experimenter.
issues.quote: If so, you were fooled... You can see how easily human memory can be distorted.

issues.description: The analysis plan uses ANOVA for 'number of correct answers.' With only 4 or 8 items, these counts are likely to be non-normal (e.g., Poisson or binomial), violating ANOVA assumptions.
issues.quote: The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA.

issues.description: The DRM word lists are not provided, nor is it stated if they have been validated in the language of the participants (Polish).
issues.quote: Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.

issues.description: The text lists four indices for the memory test but then mentions 'average accuracy' and 'overall number of answers' without defining how accuracy is calculated relative to the 'other' and 'misinformation' categories.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived... (1) correct answers... (2) answers consistent with misinformation... (3) other answers... (4) overall number.

issues.description: The first filler task is 15 minutes, while the second is 5 minutes. There is no rationale provided for this discrepancy in delay, which could affect memory decay differently across phases.
issues.quote: engaged in a filler task (solving logic puzzles) for 15 minutes... another filler task: the participants will be asked to work on multiplication problems for five minutes.

issues.description: The manuscript does not specify if pairs will be matched by gender or if they will be strangers/acquaintances, both of which are known to significantly impact memory conformity.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).

issues.description: The plan mentions 'follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups' but does not specify if or how alpha levels will be adjusted for multiple comparisons (e.g., Bonferroni).
issues.quote: In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.description: The 'Education' intervention is a 7-minute podcast. It is questionable whether such a brief, passive exposure can effectively improve metacognitive monitoring or 'mindfulness' as claimed.
issues.quote: The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... A lecture on memory may induce some kind of mindfulness.

issues.description: The manuscript refers to Figure 1 and Figure 2, but the content of Figure 2 is missing from the text, making it harder to verify the procedural flow.
issues.quote: Figure 2. An overview of the procedure.

issues.description: The power analysis relies on a joint effect size (1.13) from only two studies with vastly different results (1.92 vs 0.38). This is a highly unstable estimate for powering a new study.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92... and Hedges’ g = 0.38... joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.description: If participants fail to reach an agreement during discussion, 'both responses will be documented.' It is unclear how this is handled in the final analysis of 'misleading' exposure.
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented.
